voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: One customer wrote: my loan payoff was met and exceeded, by four daily payments. Three thousand, four hundred eighty dollars.

It's quoted in an FTC lawsuit, filed August twenty twenty, against a merchant cash advance company: Yellowstone Capital. Businesses repaid through automatic withdrawals from their bank accounts. Every day.
Since at least twenty fifteen, the FTC alleged, the withdrawals kept going after businesses paid in full. Four or five extra payments, or more.
The company told one customer: there is a four day lag on ACH debits. It's simply the way our processor works.

When one customer complained about overpayments and overdraft fees, a servicer said to throw her the hundred dollars to go away. The operations manager: money well spent, if you don't have to talk to her.

In twenty twenty-one, the defendants settled without admitting or denying it: a nine point eight million dollar judgment, and a ban on withdrawals without express informed consent. In the FTC's telling, the lag made the extra payments. And the company knew.
